items.title: Buzzy Williams Interview, 1980-06-18
items.q: I was living at the Bush Hotel with another piano player named Kid Ross... Kid Ross was turned out to be a good friend of mine

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah, I know that. A dollar and a half, a dollar and a half a week. Yeah. He introduced me to red beans and rice at the Chinamans for a nickel. I swear. China's eating in the world. And they sold, they sold two, two pork chops for a dime. Well, they used to go in Martins, in the alley, and have a big piece of roast beef there. They'd give you one slice of bread cutting and put that roast beef on it. And they had free lunch, free lunch, a bunch of cheese and stuff and stuff. And there comes along a fellow…
When Gus Wick opened up, we had a makeup box.

items.title: Buzzy Williams Interview, 1980-06-18
items.q: And Kid Ross was turned out to be a good friend of mine, see? And he was a black key artist.

ctx.x: And so that night, well, Kid Ross took me over the hotel and I got a good clean-up, see? I must have been dirty behind the ears from those trains and stuff. And Kid Ross was turned out to be a good friend of mine, see? And he was a black key artist. He played a nice piano. Black key artist. And one night they're playing, they're playing hearts. She didn't come down, let's say, go, Professor, Professor, the nigga made, Professor. And Kid Ross was playing Josie Allentons. And Kid says, go on up there. I said, oh,…
I was younger. I was younger. I was younger. I was younger. I was younger. I was younger.
